'''Alan J. Friedman''' (November 14, 1942 &ndash; May 4, 2014) was a [[physicist]] who was director of the [[New York Hall of Science]] (NYSCI) for 22 years.<ref name="sciamer">{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/the-man-who-saved-museums/|title=The Man Who Saved Museums|last=Fischer|first=Ned Potter & Stuart|work=Scientific American Blog Network|access-date=October 1, 2017|language=en|archive-date=January 18, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118201931/https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/the-man-who-saved-museums/|url-status=live}}</ref> He died of [[pancreatic cancer]] at the age of 71.<ref name="nytimes">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/07/nyregion/alan-friedman-71-dies-revived-hall-of-science.html|title=Alan J. Friedman, Who Revived Hall of Science in Queens, Dies at 71|last=Weber|first=Bruce|date=May 6, 2014|work=The New York Times|access-date=October 1, 2017|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=January 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116134357/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/07/nyregion/alan-friedman-71-dies-revived-hall-of-science.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Friedman received the 1996 Award for the Public Understanding of Science and Technology from the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AAAS Mani L. Bhaumik Award for Public Engagement with Science Recipients |url=https://www.aaas.org/awards/public-engagement-science/recipients |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |language=en}}</ref>
